deed: פרדיננד כהן סיווג את החיידקים ב-1872 והיה מאבות מדע החיידקים
title: Ferdinand Cohn, a Jewish botanist from Breslau, arranged bacteria by their shape in 1872

trailer.text: Ferdinand Julius Cohn (1828–1898), a German botanist, is recognized as one of the founders of modern bacteriology.
His Jewish parents lived in Breslau's Jewish ghetto. He remained Jewish all his life and refused to convert, even when doing so could have advanced his career.
In 1872 he published a new system for classifying bacteria by their shape, which gave microbiologists a more standardized nomenclature with which to work.
Cohn was also responsible for the publication of Robert Koch's work on the anthrax bacillus, and Koch publicly acknowledged that he was influenced by him.
According to the encyclopedia, the golden age of bacteriology in the 80s was built in part on Cohn's discoveries and on his classification system.

stations.title: A child in the Breslau ghetto

paragraphs.text: Ferdinand Julius Cohn was the eldest son of Isaac and Amalie (Nissen) Cohn, in Breslau, Silesia.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia and the Encyclopædia Universalis, he was born on January 24, 1828.
According to the Encyclopædia Universalis, his father was a Jewish merchant.
His parents lived in Breslau's Jewish ghetto with few financial means.
Their situation changed when they set up a business selling rapeseed oil for lamps.
The child learned to read at the age of two and began to study natural history at the age of four.
At the age of ten, he developed a hearing impairment.
The partial deafness stayed with him all his life.

stations.title: The door closed to a Jewish student

paragraphs.text: Cohn was admitted to the University of Breslau at a very young age. The sources disagree on whether he was then 14 or 16.
At that time the restrictions on Jews had been partly eased, yet he was not allowed to sit the degree examination at the university.
The government denied his petition to remove the restriction, and he moved to the University of Berlin.
According to the ADB, the move took place in 1846, because Jews were not then permitted to study for a doctorate in Breslau.
On November 13, 1847, at age 19, he completed a doctorate in botany in Berlin.
In October 1850 Cohn was accepted as a Privatdozent, but because he was a Jew, a year passed before he was allowed to take the oath and to teach.
Cohn refused to convert, even when doing so could have advanced his career and eased his acceptance in the scientific community.
He remained formally Jewish all his life.

stations.title: Bacteria move to the plant kingdom

paragraphs.text: According to the encyclopedia, in his work on the development of microscopic algae and fungi, Cohn placed bacteria in the plant kingdom rather than the animal kingdom, opposing previous investigators.
The sources disagree on the year in which the work appeared.
According to The Jewish Press, Cohn was the first scientist to believe that bacteria should be classified as plants.
According to the ADB, Cohn first proved that bacteria are plant organisms.
According to the Encyclopædia Universalis, Cohn began to study bacteria around 1868.
According to the same source, his contemporaries, among them Pasteur, were at that time content with arbitrary and imprecise names.
Cohn criticized Louis Pasteur for using many different names for the same microorganisms.
In the 60s and 70s of the 19th century, Cohn called for clarity in the use of names, and supported the view that bacterial species are fixed.

stations.title: An institute for plants in Breslau

paragraphs.text: According to the encyclopedia and the Encyclopædia Universalis, in 1859 Cohn was promoted to extraordinary professor of botany.
In the early 1870s he became full professor; the sources disagree on the year.
In 1866 Cohn convinced his university to establish an institute of plant physiology, which he directed.
According to the Encyclopædia Universalis, it was the first institute of its kind in the world.
At first the institute was housed in cramped quarters, and in 1888 it moved to a new and stately building.
With the opening of the Botanical Institute, which was built mainly through his efforts, Cohn received the title Geheimer Regierungsrat.
In 1872 Cohn published his classification system for bacteria.
According to the Garrison-Morton list, this was the work "Untersuchungen über Bacterien", a classification of bacteria by their shape.
In the 70s of the 19th century, microscopes and staining methods were not yet developed, so Cohn built the system on traits of form.
According to The Jewish Press, Cohn divided bacteria into four groups by shape: spheres, short rods, threads and spirals.
According to the same source, this ordering is still in use.
According to the encyclopedia, the first group, the round one, contained the genus Micrococcus, and the second, rod-shaped, contained the genus Bacterium.
According to the Encyclopædia Universalis, Cohn distinguished six genera of bacteria, which were divided into species.
The system gave microbiologists a more standardized nomenclature with which to work.
Cohn's proposal that bacteria can be arranged in genera and species helped to found the study of bacteriology.
According to the ADB of 1903, Cohn's system, built on morphological features, is still valid.
The sources disagree on whether this was the first classification system for bacteria.
Cohn founded the journal Beiträge zur Biologie der Pflanzen and edited it from 1875 until his death.
According to The Jewish Press, the journal included the first robust classification of bacteria based on their shape.
Cohn drew on the work of Roberts and was the first to discover that some bacteria have a life cycle that includes a spore stage.
He recognized that the bacterium produces highly resistant spores.
This explained why attempts at sterilization by heating sometimes failed.
The discovery of endospores justified the importance of sterilization techniques.
Cohn's 1876 paper on Bacillus subtilis inspired Tyndall's line of investigation.
Tyndall used the discovery to develop a process of discontinuous heating, which killed bacteria and their spores.
According to the ADB, Cohn definitively rejected the possibility of spontaneous generation.
Cohn also wrote a popular article, in poetic language and with exploring questions.
The article introduced bacteria and their important role in all life to a wide public.
In 1876 Robert Koch visited Cohn for several days to demonstrate his claim that the bacterium Bacillus anthracis causes the disease anthrax.

According to the entry on Cohn in the Allgemeine Deutsche Biographie (1903), it is "known" that Robert Koch, then still a district physician in Wollstein, worked in Cohn's laboratory in Breslau and discovered the anthrax bacillus there.
According to the Encyclopædia Universalis, Koch, then unknown, published his famous paper on Bacillus anthracis in Cohn's journal after the meeting.
Cohn was responsible for the publication of Koch's work on the life cycle of the anthrax bacillus.
Koch publicly acknowledged that he was influenced by Cohn.
According to the encyclopedia, the golden age of bacteriology in the 80s was built in part on Cohn's discoveries in the life cycles of bacteria and on his classification system.
According to the ADB, a new era in the scientific study of bacteria began with Cohn.
According to the same source, Cohn created the right research methods for the study of bacteria.
According to the Encyclopædia Universalis, Cohn was recognized in his lifetime as the greatest bacteriologist of his time.
He was elected a member of scientific institutions and societies, among them the Leopoldina Academy (in 1849) and the Royal Academy of Sciences of Berlin.
In 1897 fifty years had passed since his doctorate, and he received many tokens of appreciation from colleagues in his own country and abroad.
For his seventieth birthday he received the honorary freedom of the city of Breslau.
According to The Jewish Press, Cohn is considered the father of modern bacteriology.
According to the same source, he was less famous than Pasteur and Koch because he worked on the classification of bacteria and drew less public attention.
The sources disagree on how many publications he left behind.
Cohn was buried in the row of honor in the Jewish cemetery of Breslau.
According to Encyclopedia.com, Cohn died in Breslau on June 25, 1898.

versions.says: According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, in 1872

disagreements.question: Was this the first classification system for bacteria?

versions.says: According to Science and Its Times, Cohn constructed the first classification system for bacteria in the 70s of the 19th century.
According to the Encyclopædia Universalis, Cohn was the first to classify bacteria by their morphology and micro-anatomy, within the categories of the classification of living things

According to another article in the encyclopedia, Cohn was not the first: Otto Friedrich Müller built a system that included bacteria in the late 18th century, and Christian Ehrenberg, later Cohn's teacher, expanded it

According to The Jewish Press, nearly two hundred research reports, papers and books

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה אוניברסליס, כהן סיווג לראשונה גופי חיידקים לפי מורפולוגיה ומיקרו-אנטומיה, בקטגוריות של הסיסטמטיקה של היצורים החיים.
claims.quote: il utilisa ses observations au microscope pour classer, pour la première fois, selon leur morphologie et leur micro-anatomie

claims.text: לפי Jewish Press, ה-Beiträge של כהן, שהחל להתפרסם ב-1870, כלל את הסיווג המהימן הראשון של חיידקים על בסיס מורפולוגי.
claims.quote: included the first robust classification of bacteria based on morphological criteria, and his most famous discovery, documented in 1876, concerned the bacterium later known as Bacillus subtilis.

claims.text: כהן, בהסתמך על עבודתו של רוברטס, היה הראשון שגילה שלחיידקים מסוימים יש מחזור חיים הכולל שלב של נבגים.
claims.quote: Cohn, drawing on Robert's work, was the first to discover that some bacteria possess a life cycle that includes a spore stage.

claims.text: כהן זיהה שהחיידק יוצר נבגים עמידים מאוד, מה שהסביר מדוע ניסיונות עיקור בחימום נכשלו לעיתים.
claims.quote: Cohn recognized that the organism produced highly resistant spores, which explained why attempts at sterilization by heating sometimes failed

claims.text: כהן גילה את קיומם של אנדוספורות חיידקיות, ובכך הצדיק את חשיבות טכניקות הסטריליזציה.
claims.quote: Il a découvert l'existence des endospores bactériennes, justifiant ainsi l'importance des techniques de stérilisation

claims.text: מאמרו של כהן מ-1876 על Bacillus subtilis היווה השראה לקו המחקר של טינדל.
claims.quote: It was Cohn's paper on Bacillus subtilis (1876) that inspired this line of investigation for Tyndall.

claims.text: טינדל שילב את גילוי כהן ופיתח תהליך של חימום לסירוגין שהרג בהצלחה חיידקים ונבגיהם.
claims.quote: Tyndall incorporated Cohn's discovery to invent a process of discontinuous heating, which successfully killed bacteria and their spores.

claims.text: לפי ה-ADB, כהן דחה סופית את האפשרות של יצירה ספונטנית.
claims.quote: von Nägeli verfochtene Möglichkeit der Urzeugung ist durch C. endgültig abgewiesen worden.

claims.text: מאמרו הפופולרי של כהן, בשפה פואטית ובשאלות חוקרות, הציג לציבור הרחב את החיידקים ואת תפקידם החשוב בכל החיים.
claims.quote: Cohn's article, with its poetic language and its exploring questions, introduced the bacteria and their still unknown, yet crucial role in all life, to a wide public audience.

claims.text: רוברט קוך ביקר אצל כהן כמה ימים ב-1876 כדי להדגים את טענתו שהחיידק Bacillus anthracis גורם למחלת האנתרקס.
claims.quote: Koch visited Cohn for several days in 1876, in order to demonstrate his claim that the bacteria Bacillus anthracis was the cause of the disease anthrax.

claims.text: רוברט קוך עבד במעבדה של כהן בברסלאו וגילה שם את חיידק האנתרקס.
claims.quote: Es ist bekannt, daß Robert Koch, damals noch Kreisphysikus in Wollstein, hier gearbeitet und den Milzbrandbacillus entdeckt hat.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה אוניברסליס, קוך, שהיה אז בלתי מוכר, פרסם ב-Cohn's Beiträge את מאמרו המפורסם על תפקיד Bacillus anthracis במחלת האנתרקס, לאחר שפגש את כהן.
claims.quote: C'est dans Cohn's Beiträge que Robert Koch, alors inconnu, put faire paraître

claims.text: לפי ה-ADB, מכהן והלאה החל עידן חדש בחקר המדעי של החיידקים.
claims.quote: Von ihm datirt eine neue Aera in der wissenschaftlichen Untersuchung dieser winzigen Organismen.

claims.text: לפי ה-ADB, כהן יצר את שיטות המחקר הנכונות לחקר חיידקים.
claims.quote: Sein Hauptarbeitsgebiet blieben die niederen Organismen, besonders die Bakterien, für welche er die richtigen Untersuchungsmethoden erst geschaffen hat.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה אוניברסליס, כהן הוכר בחייו כגדול הבקטריולוגים של זמנו.
claims.quote: Cohn fut reconnu, de son vivant, comme le plus grand bactériologiste de son temps.

claims.text: כהן נבחר לחבר במוסדות ובאגודות מדעיות, ובהן האקדמיה לופולדינה והאקדמיה המלכותית למדעים של ברלין.
claims.quote: He was elected a member of the following institutions and societies: Leopold Carolinische Akademie, Royal Academy of Sciences of Berlin

claims.text: יובל החמישים לדוקטורט של כהן ב-1897 הביא לו הוכחות רבות להערכה מצד עמיתים בארץ ובחו"ל.
claims.quote: Das fünfzigjährige Doctorjubiläum 1897 brachte dem verdienten Gelehrten vielfache Beweise der Anerkennung der Fachgenossen des In- und Auslandes

claims.text: לפי Jewish Press, כהן נחשב לאביה של הבקטריולוגיה המודרנית ולאחד ממייסדיה החשובים ביותר.
claims.quote: Considered the father of modern bacteriology and among its most significant founders

claims.text: לפי Jewish Press, כהן היה פחות מפורסם מפסטר וקוך משום שעסק בסיווג חיידקים ולכן משך פחות תשומת לב ציבורית.
claims.quote: Although Cohn (1828-1898) was not as famous as Pasteur and Robert Koch because he worked on the classification of bacteria

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, כהן השאיר אחריו למעלה מ-150 מאמרים, חיבורים וספרים.
claims.quote: Cohn was a prolific writer; leaving behind him over 150 papers, essays, and books

claims.text: לפי מאמר ב-Jewish Press, כהן פרסם כמעט מאתיים דוחות מחקר, מאמרים וספרים במהלך חייו.
claims.quote: he published nearly two hundred research reports, papers, essays, and books during his lifetime

claims.text: כהן נקבר בשורת הכבוד בבית הקברות היהודי של ברסלאו.
claims.quote: Cohn was buried in the row of honor in the Jewish cemetery of Breslau.

claims.text: לפי Encyclopedia.com, כהן מת בברסלאו ב-25 ביוני 1898.
claims.quote: Cohn died in Breslau on June 25, 1898
